messages.author: dd64ceb2fecfeb1b
messages.subject: Error in ddf.obj during dsm()
parts:
Hi all, 

I am in the process of running DSM analyses for several terrestrial species using line transect data.  I have successfully completed the analysis for 4 species, but for the current species I am getting an error message during the dsm() call which I have not seen before (and I don't think I have done anything different/unusual).  

I have run a whole bunch of ds(), and compared DF models and selected my model.  My DF model is as follows:

ycgDF.hr.cov4 <- ds(ycg_distdata, truncation = 50, key = "hn", formula = ~year)

I then try the dsm() call as follows:

ycgDSM.sat <- dsm(Nhat ~ s(dstWater,bs="ts")+ s(dstStlmnt,bs="ts")+ s(dstRoad,bs="ts")+ s(dstBorder,bs="ts")+ s(dstStation,bs="ts")+ s(elevation,bs="ts")+ habitat,
                                 ycgDF.hn.cov4, segdata, ycg_obsdata, method = "REML", family = quasipoisson(link = "log"), 
                                 engine = "gam", segment.area = segdata$Sample.Area, group = TRUE)

I get the following error:

Error in !ddf.obj$meta.data$point : invalid argument type

I have inspected the DF object, specifically looking at ycgDF.hr.cov4$ddf$meta.data$point, as per the error message, and the class of that slot is "logical", and it is FALSE.  I have checked other DF objects which do work, and they are exactly the same, so I am not sure what the problem is.

Any advice would be much appreciated!

Cheers
Matt

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error in ddf.obj during dsm()
parts:
Matt

Thanks for all the digging you've done to diagnose the problem.    Not at all clear what the problem might be given you can successfully analyse data for other species.  The error comes from a check whether line transect or point transect data were being analysed.  The addition of point transect data in dsm is fairly recent, and requires version 2.2.0 of the mrds package.  There is a chance you have gotten inconsistency in your R packages (Distance, mrds, dsm) or your detection function objects may have been produced with an earlier version of packages.

I suggest you double check that your packages are current and if necessary, re-run the detection function fitting. It's a bit of a stretch, but the best guess I have.  Maybe others have smarter suggestions.

Eric Rexstad

messages.author: dd64ceb2fecfeb1b
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error in ddf.obj during dsm()
parts:
Hi Eric, many thanks for the quick response.  

I checked and my version of Distance wasn't the latest, and so I updated that, but it didn't seem to make a difference.  However, I have managed to solve the problem (without really knowing the exact cause):

I have been using a very basic function in order to speed up the coding and running of lots of detection function models, and this seems to be where the problem lies.  The function looks like this:

detfunc <- function(dat,key,covar) {
  
  name <- ds(data=dat, truncation = 50, key=key, formula = covar)
  
  par(mfrow=c(1,2))
  plot(name, showpoints=FALSE, pl.den=0, lwd=2)
  ddf.gof(name$ddf)
  summary(name)
}

which allows me to code my multiple models like so:

ycgDF.hn.cov2 <- detfunc(ycg_distdata,"hn",~habitat)
ycgDF.hr.cov3 <- detfunc(ycg_distdata,"hr",~transect)
ycgDF.hn.cov4 <- detfunc(ycg_distdata,"hn",~NameObserver)
...etc

For the models that were causing the error, if I run the model outside of the function, using the normal code i.e.:

ycgDF.hr.cov3 <- ds(ycg_distdata, truncation = 50, formula = ~transect)

Then it works!  So the function is doing something odd.  What is strange is that the function and it's output works fine for models that have no covariates. 

I think the moral of the story is don't try to be too clever. The function wasn't really speeding anything up anyway to be honest.  But hopefully now all will be well, I will just scrap using the function.

Thanks again for getting back to me.

Matt
